notes: All TDLib request/reply payload shapes in these five files were checked against tdlib/td/td/generate/scheme/td_api.tl and are correct (field names, int53 vs int32, nullable InputChatPhoto, bytes-as-base64 for reportChat option_id). All completions are delivered on the main queue by -[TGClient handleUpdate:] (TGClient.m:102,146,163), so the __block counters in tg_fetchUsers/tg_fetchChats are safe and the many `__weak typeof(self)` guards are moot (TGClient is a never-deallocated singleton). No int64 truncation via integerValue was found on any chat/user id in this area. The real damage here is a wrong privacy-rule parse, a synchronous secret-chat predicate that lies on first call, and roughly 1500 lines of unreachable parallel implementations.

findings.what: -privacyRuleDetailed:completion: latches its base-value flag on ANY unrecognised rule type: `else if (!haveBase){ haveBase = YES; if ([type isEqualToString:@"userPrivacySettingRuleAllowAll"]) value = @"everybody"; else if ([type isEqualToString:@"userPrivacySettingRuleAllowContacts"]) value = @"contacts"; }` — haveBase is set to YES before the type is known to be one of the three handled shapes, so the real base rule that follows is skipped and `value` keeps its @"nobody" default.
findings.failure: td_api.tl:8841-8871 defines eleven rule types; four of them are not handled by any branch here (userPrivacySettingRuleAllowBots, userPrivacySettingRuleAllowPremiumUsers, userPrivacySettingRuleRestrictContacts, userPrivacySettingRuleRestrictBots). TDLib returns rules most-specific-first, so a Last Seen setting of 'Everybody except bots' comes back as [RestrictBots, AllowAll]. RestrictBots hits the else-if, sets haveBase=YES, and AllowAll is then ignored: privacyRuleDetailed reports value="nobody". TGPrivacyViewController.m:1094-1100 stores that into strongSelf.value and shows a checkmark on 'Nobody'. When the user then taps 'Contacts' (TGPrivacyViewController.m:1212) the app writes [RestrictUsers?, AllowContacts] and the RestrictBots rule the user had is destroyed — a privacy setting silently downgraded from a misread. The sibling implementation in TGClient+UserStatus.m:311-322 does this correctly (it only sets haveValue inside a matched branch), so the two files disagree about the same reply.
findings.fix: Move `haveBase = YES;` inside each of the three matched branches, exactly as TGClient+UserStatus.m:311-322 does: `else if (!haveBase){ if ([type isEqualToString:@"userPrivacySettingRuleAllowAll"]){ value = @"everybody"; haveBase = YES; } else if ([type isEqualToString:@"userPrivacySettingRuleAllowContacts"]){ value = @"contacts"; haveBase = YES; } else if ([type isEqualToString:@"userPrivacySettingRuleRestrictAll"]){ value = @"nobody"; haveBase = YES; } }`.

findings.what: -secretChatIdForChat: is a synchronous predicate backed by an asynchronously-filled cache and returns 0 on every cache miss: `NSNumber *known = TGSecretChatIds()[@(chatId)]; if (known) return [known intValue]; [self tgSecretFetchChat:chatId completion:nil]; return 0;`. The cache (TGSecretChatIds, line 4) is only ever written by -tgSecretRemember: from tgSecretFetchChat/createSecretChatWithUser/openSecretChatId, so a secret chat that exists on the server but has not been touched this launch always answers 'not a secret chat' the first time.
findings.failure: Two live call sites are wrong on first use. (1) TGChatListViewController.m:1973 `if (!chatId || [[TGClient shared] secretChatIdForChat:chatId] == 0) return nil;` — after a cold launch every secret chat row renders with no handshake line ('waiting for X to come online' / 'exchanging encryption keys'), and because the method bails before the row is added to self.secretStatusesRequested nothing schedules a redraw; the line only appears if some unrelated event reloads the table later. (2) TGProfileViewController.m:693 `if (!self.chatId || ![[TGClient shared] isSecretChat:self.chatId]) [items addObject:@{@"title":@"Start secret chat"...}]` — opening the profile of an existing secret chat for the first time offers 'Start secret chat', and tapping it (TGProfileViewController.m:1489) calls createNewSecretChat and creates a duplicate second secret chat with the same user.
findings.fix: Make the predicate honest and asynchronous, or prime the cache. Minimum fix: seed TGSecretChatIds from chat objects the client already has — call -tgSecretRemember: from TGClient's updateNewChat/updateChatLastMessage handling in TGClient.m -handleUpdate:, so every chat that appears in the chat list is classified before any row is drawn. Additionally, in TGChatListViewController.m:1973, when secretChatIdForChat: misses, do not `return nil` silently — the -tgSecretFetchChat: it kicks off should call back and trigger `[me.tableView reloadData]`; give tgSecretFetchChat a completion that posts a notification the chat list observes.

findings.what: Three parallel privacy-rule APIs exist and two of them are wired to different screens: TGClient.m:2028 -privacyRule:completion: / TGClient.m:2046 -setPrivacyRule:to: (base rule only, fire-and-forget), TGClient+UserStatus.m:274/334 -privacyRuleDetail:completion: / -setPrivacyRule:to:allowUsers:restrictUsers:completion: (unused), and TGClient+Privacy.m:111/162 -privacyRuleDetailed:completion: / -setPrivacyRule:to:allowedUsers:restrictedUsers:completion:.
findings.failure: TGSettingsViewController.m:2373 calls `[[TGClient shared] setPrivacyRule:setting to:value]` — TGClient.m:2046 builds `@"rules" : @[@{@"@type" : rule}]`, a one-element list with only the base rule. setUserPrivacySettingRules replaces the entire rule list, so any AllowUsers/RestrictUsers exception list the user built on the Privacy screen (TGPrivacyViewController.m:1212, which does pass them) is deleted server-side. Concretely: add five people to 'Never share my Last Seen', go back to Settings and flip Last Seen from Everybody to My Contacts, and all five exceptions are gone with no warning. TGClient.m:2036 `[rules[@"rules"] firstObject][@"@type"]` compounds it by reporting 'nobody' whenever the first rule is a RestrictUsers exception.
findings.fix: Delete -privacyRule:completion: and -setPrivacyRule:to: from TGClient.m:2028-2058 (and their declarations at TGClient.h:212-214) and delete -privacyRuleDetail:completion: / -setPrivacyRule:to:allowUsers:restrictUsers:completion: from TGClient+UserStatus.m:274-363 (declarations at TGClient+UserStatus.h:69,77). Point TGSettingsViewController.m:508 at -privacyRuleDetailed:completion: (reading info[@"value"]) and TGSettingsViewController.m:2373 at -setPrivacyRule:to:allowedUsers:restrictedUsers:completion:, passing the allowedUserIds/restrictedUserIds it just read back unchanged so the exception lists survive.

Verified unreferenced outside the file: -countriesWithCompletion: (155), -guessedCountryCodeWithCompletion: (185), -phoneNumberInfo:completion: (198), -preferredLanguageForCountry:completion: (224), -startLoginWithPhoneNumber:isCurrentNumber:completion: (243), -registrationTermsWithCompletion: (315), -registerWithFirstName:lastName:completion: (334), -acceptTermsOfService:completion: (348), -confirmQrCodeLogin:completion: (401) together with its only helper TGAccountSessionDict (128), all four -sendChangePhoneNumberCode:/-checkChangePhoneNumberCode:/-resendChangePhoneNumberCodeWithCompletion:/-reportChangePhoneNumberCodeMissing: (525-578), -setLoginEmailAddress: (582), -resendLoginEmailAddressCodeWithCompletion: (600), -checkLoginEmailAddressCode: (615), the three generic email-verification methods (627-668), -usernamesWithCompletion: (672), -setUsername:active: (707), -reorderActiveUsernames: (720), -setProfilePhotoAtPath: (735), -profilePhotosWithCompletion: (754), -deleteProfilePhoto: (811), -publicLinkWithCompletion: (821), -searchUserByToken: (835), -setBirthdateDay:month:year: (861), -clearBirthdateWithCompletion: (884), -setPersonalChat: (891), -accountInfoWithCompletion: (960), -profileInfoWithCompletion: (972), -setFirstName:lastName: (1000), -setBio:completion: (1018), -setAccountTtlDays:completion: (1028), -currentSessionWithCompletion: (1046), -logOutWithCompletion: (1089).
findings.failure: TGLoginViewController.m only uses the email/QR/recovery methods (lines 691-1220); it sends the phone number through TGClient.m's own path and calls `[[TGClient shared] logOut]` (TGLoginViewController.m:1146), not -logOutWithCompletion:. The profile screens use TGClient.m:1559 -setName:last:, TGClient.m:1567 -setBio: and TGClient.m:2089 -setAccountTtlDays: — the fire-and-forget variants that report no error — so TGEditProfileViewController cannot tell the user a name or bio change failed, while the completion-carrying category versions right here sit unused. On a 512MB iPhone 4S this is ~600 lines of __TEXT plus every literal NSDictionary in it, loaded and never executed.
findings.fix: Delete the listed methods and their declarations in TGClient+Account.h, keeping only what TGLoginViewController.m actually calls: -authenticationCodeInfoWithCompletion:, -resendAuthenticationCodeWithFailureMessage:completion:, -reportAuthenticationCodeMissing:completion:, -requestQrCodeLoginWithCompletion:, -qrCodeLoginLinkWithCompletion:, -setAuthenticationEmailAddress:completion:, -checkAuthenticationEmailCode:completion:, -authenticationEmailStateWithCompletion:, -resetAuthenticationEmailAddressWithCompletion:, the three requestAuthentication/checkAuthentication/recoverAuthentication password-recovery methods, plus -sessionInfoForId:completion: (TGSessionsViewController.m:764) and the private -authorizationStateOfType:completion: and -pollQrCodeLinkWithAttemptsLeft:completion: helpers. Before deleting -setFirstName:lastName:completion: / -setBio:completion: / -setAccountTtlDays:completion:, consider the opposite move: switch TGEditProfileViewController and TGSettingsViewController to these and delete TGClient.m:1559/1567/2089 instead, so failures surface.

findings.what: The user-status text engine exists three times. +[TGClient statusInfoForUserStatus:] (TGClient+UserStatus.m:108) with its TGUSLastSeenText helper (line 36) is the most complete version — today/yesterday/weekday/date, rank, hiddenByMyPrivacy — and has zero callers. TGClient.m:590-603 and TGClient.m:1725-1755 each contain their own, cruder, 'last seen ...' formatters, and those are the ones the screens actually see.
findings.failure: grep for 'last seen' across src/ returns hits only in TGClient.m (lines 594, 598, 600, 602, 603, 1729, 1731, 1733, 1747, 1748, 1753) and in TGClient+UserStatus.m itself; nothing outside the category references statusInfoForUserStatus:, statusInfoForUser: or hiddenStatusHintForStatusInfo:. So the app ships the weaker text ('last seen at 14:03' with no day qualifier, TGClient.m:1747) and silently drops the userStatusRecently by_my_privacy_settings hint that TGClient+UserStatus.m:160-169 was written to explain. Two of the three will drift apart on the next edit.
findings.fix: Delete the formatters at TGClient.m:588-603 and TGClient.m:1725-1755 and have both call sites use +[TGClient statusInfoForUserStatus:], reading info[@"text"], info[@"isOnline"] and info[@"rank"] (the key names already match what TGClient.m:598-603 returns, so the call sites need only substitute the constructor).

findings.what: Three session flatteners with divergent key names: TGPrivacySessionDict (TGClient+Privacy.m:38) emits @"ip", @"lastActive" and a pre-joined @"platform" (`platform + " " + system_version`); TGAccountFlattenSession (TGClient+Account.m:935) emits @"ipAddress", @"lastActiveDate", and separate @"platform" / @"systemVersion"; TGAccountSessionDict (TGClient+Account.m:128) is a third, shorter variant using @"ip" and a %@ %@ platform string.
findings.failure: TGSessionsViewController populates its list from -activeSessionsWithCompletion: (Privacy shape) but refreshes the detail screen from -sessionInfoForId:completion: (Account shape, TGSessionsViewController.m:764). The detail screen only survives this because it defensively probes both key sets (TGSessionsViewController.m:708-730 `firstStringIn:keys:@[@"platform", @"systemVersion"]`, `@[@"ipAddress", @"ip"]`, `@[@"lastActiveDate", @"lastActive"]`). The System row still degrades: pushed from the list it reads 'iOS 6.1.3' (Privacy's joined string), and one second later -reload replaces it with 'iOS' because firstStringIn: returns Account's bare @"platform" and never appends @"systemVersion". TGAccountSessionDict is reachable only from -confirmQrCodeLogin:completion:, which has no callers at all.
findings.fix: Delete TGAccountSessionDict (TGClient+Account.m:128-142) with -confirmQrCodeLogin:completion:. Make TGPrivacySessionDict the single flattener: move it to a shared place, adopt Account's key names (@"ipAddress", @"lastActiveDate", separate @"platform"/@"systemVersion", plus @"deviceType", @"isPasswordPending", @"apiId" from TGAccountFlattenSession), have -sessionInfoForId:completion: and -currentSessionWithCompletion: call it, and change TGSessionsViewController.m:708-710 to build System as platform + " " + systemVersion instead of first-of.

findings.what: The default message-auto-delete accessors are written twice with different names and different call styles: TGClient+Privacy.m:535 -defaultAutoDeleteSecondsWithCompletion: / :548 -setDefaultAutoDeleteSeconds:completion: versus TGClient+SecretChats.m:443 -defaultAutoDeleteTimeWithCompletion: / :456 -setDefaultAutoDeleteTime: (fire-and-forget, no completion). Neither pair has a single caller anywhere in src/.
findings.failure: Both wrap the identical getDefaultMessageAutoDeleteTime / setDefaultMessageAutoDeleteTime requests. Whichever a future screen picks, the other keeps compiling and will be edited independently; the SecretChats setter additionally clamps negatives (`@(seconds < 0 ? 0 : seconds)`) while the Privacy setter does not, so the two already disagree on input validation. Also duplicated across the same two files: -setSession:canAcceptCalls:canAcceptSecrets:completion: (Privacy.m:310) vs -setSession:canAcceptSecretChats: (SecretChats.m:527), and -setCloseFriends:completion: (Contacts.m:352) vs -setCloseFriends: (Stories.m:773).
findings.fix: Delete -defaultAutoDeleteTimeWithCompletion: and -setDefaultAutoDeleteTime: from TGClient+SecretChats.m:443-464 (declarations at TGClient+SecretChats.h:134,137) and add the `seconds < 0 ? 0 : seconds` clamp to TGClient+Privacy.m:552. Delete -setSession:canAcceptSecretChats: (TGClient+SecretChats.m:527, header line 171) in favour of the Privacy pair used by TGSessionsViewController.m:906, and delete -setCloseFriends: (TGClient+Stories.m:773, header line 189) in favour of the completion-carrying TGClient+Contacts.m:352.

findings.what: -checkUsernameAvailable:completion: checks an account username using the public-chat endpoint with chat_id 0: `[self request:@{ @"@type" : @"checkChatUsername", @"chat_id" : @(0), @"username" : username }`.
findings.failure: td_api.tl:11553 documents chat_id as 'identifier of a supergroup or channel chat, or a private chat with self, or 0 if the chat is being created'. Passing 0 asks TDLib whether the name is free for a NEW PUBLIC GROUP, so the answer is filtered through the public-chat quota: a user who already owns the maximum number of public groups gets checkChatUsernameResultPublicChatsTooMany and the method reports @"too_many" for a username that is in fact perfectly available for their account, and on some accounts checkChatUsernameResultPublicGroupsUnavailable → @"unavailable". The username picker would refuse a valid name.
findings.fix: Pass the private chat with self. Fetch the own user id once (getMe → id) and use it as chat_id, or resolve the Saved Messages chat id and pass that: `@"chat_id" : @(myUserId)`. Note this method currently has no callers, so fix it at the same time as wiring up the username editor, or delete it along with the other dead Contacts methods.

findings.what: TGIsError sends isEqualToString: to an unchecked object: `return ![result isKindOfClass:NSDictionary.class] || [result[@"@type"] isEqualToString:@"error"];`. The same unguarded pattern is at TGClient+SecretChats.m:11 (TGScIsError) and at the raw comparisons in TGClient+Contacts.m:43 (`![u[@"@type"] isEqualToString:@"user"]`), :138, :274, :384 and :650.
findings.failure: If a reply ever carries a non-string under @"@type" — a corrupted frame, a future td_api change, or any object the client synthesises and passes through these helpers — the message lands on an NSNumber or NSArray and the app dies with 'unrecognized selector sent to instance'. The two sibling files in this same area already guard: TGClient+Account.m:7-10 checks `[type isKindOfClass:[NSString class]]` first and TGClient+UserStatus.m:24 routes through TGUSString. Contacts and SecretChats were written without it, so identical code has two different crash profiles.
findings.fix: In TGClient+Contacts.m:22-25 and TGClient+SecretChats.m:11-14, route the type through the file's existing string coercion, matching TGClient+UserStatus.m:22-25: `return ![result isKindOfClass:NSDictionary.class] || [TGString(result[@"@type"]) isEqualToString:@"error"];` (TGScString in SecretChats). Do the same at Contacts.m:43, :138, :274, :384 and :650, e.g. `![TGString(u[@"@type"]) isEqualToString:@"user"]`.

findings.what: -countOnlineAmong:index:running:completion: walks the member list one TDLib round trip at a time — `[self request:@{@"@type" : @"getUser", @"user_id" : @(userId)} completion:^{ ... [weakSelf countOnlineAmong:userIds index:index + 1 ...]; }]` — and -groupOnlineSummaryForChat: (line 201) feeds it up to 50 supergroup members (line 255 `@"limit" : @(50)`).
findings.failure: Fifty serialised getUser calls to produce one '128 members, 7 online' header line. Each reply is dispatch_async'd onto the main queue (TGClient.m:102), so on a single-core A5 the chat header takes tens of round trips to settle, and nothing caches the result or cancels the chain when the user leaves the chat — reopening the same group restarts all fifty. There is also no error check on the getBasicGroupFullInfo reply (line 232), so a failed lookup silently yields '0 members'.
findings.fix: Replace the per-user walk with the counts TDLib already returns: for supergroups, supergroupFullInfo carries member_count (already read at line 250) — there is no separate online count in td_api, so either drop the ', N online' suffix or bound the probe to the members already resident in the client. If the online count is kept, cache the result per chatId with a short TTL, cap the probe at ~10 members, and guard the getBasicGroupFullInfo reply with TGUSIsError(full) before calling answer().

findings.failure: Roughly 900 lines of compiled-in code no screen can reach, on a device with 40-60MB of usable RAM. Worse than the size cost: the secret-chat security surface is inert. -secretChat:allowsInputMessage: (the gate that blocks polls, checklists, forwards, stories, invoices and games in a secret chat) and -chatAllowsMessageEditing: are never consulted by the composer, and -selfDestructOptionForChat:seconds: is never attached to an outgoing message, so the self-destruct timer UI has no send path behind it. -encryptionKeyGridForChat: means there is no key-visualisation screen at all.
findings.fix: Two separate decisions. (a) Delete the contact/profile helpers that no screen plans to use, together with their declarations in TGClient+Contacts.h and TGClient+SecretChats.h. (b) Do NOT delete the secret-chat gates — wire them up: call -secretChat:allowsInputMessage: in TGChatViewController before building any non-text inputMessage content, call -chatAllowsMessageEditing: before showing the Edit action in the message menu, and merge the dictionary from -selfDestructOptionForChat:seconds: into the sendMessage payload for secret chats.
